drivingQuestion: Does the halakha follow R' Eliezer's intervals, or may students leave for years without permission?
outcomeNote: Two traditions of Rav set side by side; Rava comments on those who acted on the second

segments.he: הַסַּפָּנִים אַחַת לְשִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. אָמַר רַב בְּרוֹנָא אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: הַתַּלְמִידִים יוֹצְאִין לְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְשׁוּת. אָמַר רָבָא: סָמְכוּ רַבָּנַן אַדְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה וְעָבְדִי עוֹבָדָא בְּנַפְשַׁיְיהוּ.
segments.en: § The mishna stated: For «sailors,» the set interval for conjugal relations is «once every six months. This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer. Rav Berona said» that «Rav said:» The «halakha is in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Eliezer. Rav Adda bar Ahava said» that «Rav said: This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer, but the Rabbis say: Students may leave» their homes «to study Torah» for as long as «two or three years without permission» from their wives. «Rava said: The Sages relied on Rabbi Adda bar Ahava’s» opinion «and performed an action» like this «themselves,» but the results were sometimes fatal.
